annotation.title_en: The Africa Declaration on Artificial Intelligence
annotation.authors_or_issuer: African ministers and representatives (Global AI Summit on Africa, Kigali); Smart Africa; African Union; C4IR Rwanda
named_instruments_referenced: Smart Africa AI for Africa Blueprint
AU Convention on Cybersecurity and Personal Data Protection (Malabo)
annotation.summary_en: This is a bilingual (English/French) declaration signed by African ministers, Smart Africa and the African Union in Kigali on 4 April 2025. It sets guiding principles for AI in Africa, covering sovereignty, inclusivity, safeguards and sustainability. It commits to action on AI talent, data governance, sovereign computing, markets, sandboxes, a $60 billion Africa AI Fund and an AI council. It has no robotics content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Guiding principles of sovereignty, inclusivity, harm prevention, privacy, transparency, dignity and environmental sustainability
Continent-wide AI education and literacy programmes, plus endorsement of an African AI Scientific Panel
A framework for African open datasets and open AI models, and data governance in line with the AU Data Policy Framework
Distributed sovereign computing infrastructure, regional high-performance data centres and an 'Africa-first' approach to AI procurement using AfCFTA and regulatory sandboxes
Establishment of a $60 billion Africa AI Fund and an African AI Council
